content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a new version of a Jumo device and I'm trying to set up Modbus communication with my [product_name]. The hardware I have is a [product_name] with [article_no], running [product_name] V[version_no]. I managed to read the temperature value (AI1) from the Jumo via Modbus on the [product_name]. However, I'm unable to send a digital value (M1) from the [product_name] to the Jumo and have it recorded. During online tests, I can read bit M1=V1104.0 and M2=V1104.1, but nothing appears on the Jumo. I've also tried mapping with V100.0 and V100.1, and experimented with different datatypes and addresses. I'm not sure what I'm missing. If anyone has a solution, I'd appreciate the help. --- Split from 'Connect [product_name] to Jumo.'
If I were in your position, I'd set the [product_name] as the Modbus client and the Jumo device as the server.
It seems there may be an error in your approach. The register address 4420 is likely a holding register, not a coil address. You could try using a different address.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is facing issues sending a digital bit (M1) from their [product_name] PLC to a Jumo device over Modbus. Reading analog input values works, but writing digital values does not, raising questions about correct Modbus addresses and datatypes for writing bits.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wishes to map and send digital values from their [product_name] to a Jumo device using Modbus and have these values successfully recorded on the Jumo.
